title: Tool Definition
description: How a tool describes itself. Tools self-describe (D146) — definitions come from the tools themselves, not from manual configuration. MCP tools describe themselves via protocol, CLI tools provide manifest files, native functions are defined in code. Each definition is uniquely identified by source.id plus name. Source is provenance only; connection credentials and adapter configuration live outside this definition.

name.description: The tool's name. Tools identify themselves by source and name — an MCP server exposes a namespace, a CLI tool has a command name, a native function has a function name. Two tools named 'search' from different sources are distinguishable without a central naming authority.

description.description: Human-readable description of what the tool does. Used by the model to decide when to call this tool. Provided by the tool itself, not written by the user.

parameters.description: JSON Schema describing the tool's input parameters. The model uses this to construct valid arguments when calling the tool. Follows standard JSON Schema conventions.

type.description: Tool parameters are always an object

properties.description: Map of parameter names to their JSON Schema definitions

id.description: Stable source identity. source.id plus tool name is the unique tool identity.

kind.description: How the source exposes tools. This is provenance, not an adapter configuration contract.

source.description: Provenance supplied by the tool source. It must not contain endpoints, credentials, or runtime adapter settings.

mode.description: Owner-controlled model-context visibility. always_send includes the definition in every prompt; discoverable exposes it through discovery.

authorization.description: Auth's current-actor projection. not_permitted tools remain visible/marked so the model distinguishes unavailable permission from an unknown tool.

visibility.description: Visibility combines owner-selected context mode with Auth's per-actor permitted/not_permitted marker. It is not a permission store.

read_only.description: Descriptive capability metadata only; Auth and the tool enforce the actual action policy.

examples.name: read_file
examples.description: Read a file from the user's library. Returns the file content as text.

path.description: Path to the file to read, relative to the library root

examples.name: write_file
examples.description: Write content to a file in the user's library. Creates the file if it does not exist, overwrites if it does.

path.description: Path to the file to write

content.description: Content to write to the file

examples.name: git_commit
examples.description: Commit staged changes to the git repository with a commit message.

examples.name: memory_restore
examples.description: Make an earlier version of owner memory current again.

path.description: Path or scope whose earlier version should become current

version.description: Opaque version identifier returned by the memory history operation
